case.pattern_description: A single device profile (SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080) was used on 28 different cards between 2016-11-14 and 2016-12-04. It was recorded as new to every account it touched and sat behind an anonymising proxy on every transaction, which is not how a genuinely shared device behaves -- a household or office device shows returning users. The purchases are small and spread thinly across many cards, so no single cardholder looks alarming; the pattern is only visible as a shared-device cluster across the portfolio.

case.summary: The card’s recent online purchases all originate from a shared anonymised device that has been linked to multiple confirmed fraud cases. Low risk scores alone would not trigger a flag, but the shared‑device ring and the cardholder’s denial push the fraud probability into the high range. Policy mandates opening a case, filing a SAR, and placing all cards on this device under monitoring.

sar.narrative: The subject of the report is customer C13487 using payment card C13487‑K1. Three online purchases identified by transaction numbers 3460634, 3478561 and 3489320 totalled $439.61. The transactions occurred between 2016‑11‑15 20:30:00 and 2016‑11‑26 17:39:00. All activity was conducted via the online channel, product code C, from a Samsung SM‑G935F device running Android 7.0 with Chrome 62.0 for Android at a resolution of 1920×1080. The purchases were executed using an undocumented transaction pattern and each transaction was anonymised, with the same device profile appearing on all three events. The device profile is shared with twenty‑eight other cards, including C01289‑K1, C01996‑K2, C02910‑K1, C02975‑K1, C03676‑K2, C04108‑K2, C04274‑K1, C05448‑K2, C06031‑K2, C06650‑K2, C06710‑K1, and C07472‑K1, establishing a link to multiple accounts. When contacted, the cardholder affirmed that they did not make the purchases and that they continue to possess the card. The combination of an undocumented transaction pattern, a device profile newly associated with each affected account, and similarity to prior cases CC‑5336, CC‑5263, CC‑5217, CC‑4834 and CC‑4405 renders the activity suspicious.
